Class TextDielectricMaterial

java.lang.Object
net.murat.material.TextDielectricMaterial
All Implemented Interfaces:
Material
public class TextDielectricMaterial extends Object implements Material
TextDielectricMaterial - ULTRA OPTIMIZED Android adaptation: uses Bitmap, Canvas and Paint for texture generation.

Compatibility contract: every public constructor and method signature, the constructor parameter order and the layout of toString() are unchanged. All additions are new methods or private members.

Default behaviour ("standard mode") keeps the original look: a 1024x1024 texture, nearest-texel lookup and a hard alpha threshold between glass and ink. Optional extras, all OFF by default:

  • setHighQuality(boolean): 2048x1024 texture (matches the 2:1 sphere mapping), bilinear lookup, soft glass/ink blend and filtered image down-scaling.
  • setFullWidthGradient(boolean): the text gradient spans the whole text instead of only its first third.

Alpha handling: the alpha channel of every colour parameter is honoured.

  • Texture colours (textColor, gradientColor, bgColor, image): in standard mode a texel with alpha equal/bigger 128 is ink and is blended over the glass with its own opacity (alpha / 255); a texel with alpha less 128 stays pure glass. In high quality mode the interpolated alpha is used directly as coverage, so the whole 0..255 range works.
  • Semi-transparent ink also raises the transparency reported to the renderer, so rays continue through the pixel.
  • Filter colours: their alpha scales the tint strength. For backwards compatibility an alpha of 0 (the old 0xRRGGBB style) is treated as fully opaque; use at least 0x01 to get a real alpha. The same rule applies to diffuseColor when no texture exists.

Dielectric filters (filterColorInside / filterColorOutside) are always active: on glass pixels the colour is blended toward the filter colour, on ink pixels (text, image, bgColor) a gentle multiplicative tint is applied so detail and sharpness are preserved.

Thread safety: shading uses no shared mutable scratch state, so one instance may be shared by several render threads. Setters that rebuild the texture or change tuning values must be called before rendering starts.

    • toString

      public String toString()
      Layout of the original properties is unchanged. transparency / reflectivity print the configured material values instead of whatever the last rendered pixel happened to compute, so a saved scene reloads with the values that were originally set. The optional extras (highQuality, fullWidthGradient, filter tuning) are appended after filterColorOutside and only when they differ from their defaults.
